lore_summary.en: The Arsacids rule in fragments. Many small kings, many small wars. The chronicle dims between golden ages.
lore_summary.fa: دوران اشکانیان پانصد سال تاریخ است که فردوسی صادقانه اعتراف می‌کند که روایاتش پراکنده شده. چهارده شاه را نام می‌برد اما داستان‌هایشان به دستش نرسیده. اشکانیان ایران را زنده نگه داشتند و روم را شکست دادند، اما سکوت شاهنامه درباره آنها خود یکی از صادقانه‌ترین لحظات حماسه است.

scenes.body_en: There is a moment in the Shahnameh where Ferdowsi stops and admits that the records are gone. The Ashkanian age — five centuries of the Arsacid dynasty ruling Iran — survives in the poem as a kind of acknowledged silence. He lists fourteen kings. He gives them names and rough lengths of reign. And then he says, plainly, that their stories were not written down or that what was written did not reach him. The chronicle of a dynasty four hundred years long fits in a few pages.

This is not failure on Ferdowsi's part. It is honesty. The Arsacids ruled a decentralized empire — Iran split into regional kingdoms, each with its own court, its own records, its own version of events. The Zoroastrian priesthood that had preserved the old royal histories under the Achaemenids had been disrupted. The Seleucid interlude between Alexander and the Arsacids had broken the chain of transmission. What came through was fragments, and Ferdowsi refused to fill the gaps with invention.

What he does preserve carries its own weight. The Ashkanian kings held Iran together under a loose sovereignty while the old Persian culture slowly reasserted itself. They held Rome at Carrhae and humbled a superpower. They built a world where the idea of Iran — the Aryan lands, the heir of the Kayanian kings — survived the Greek interruption and waited for something to reclaim it fully. The Sasanians would say they were that something. But the Ashkanians made the ground for them.

The chapter ends not with a battle but with an absence. Ferdowsi acknowledges the silence and moves forward. There is a kind of dignity in refusing to pretend that what was lost can be recovered. He had spent thirty years reconstructing the memory of Iran. Here the memory had genuinely not survived, and he let the gap stand. It is one of the most honest moments in the poem.

battle.intro_en: The Arsacid era is the Shahnameh's briefest: many kings, many wars, thin chronicle. Ferdowsi names the age but does not dwell. To face this gate you must understand why the Shahnameh rushes through four centuries.
battle.intro_fa: دوره‌ی اشکانی کوتاه‌ترینِ شاهنامه است: شاهانِ بسیار، جنگ‌هایِ بسیار، روایتِ کم. فردوسی عصر را نام می‌برد اما درنگ نمی‌کند. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید بفهمی چرا شاهنامه از چهار سده می‌گذرد.

battle.intro_tg: Давраи Ашкониён кӯтоҳтарини Шоҳнома аст: шоҳони бисёр, ҷангҳои бисёр, ривояти кам. Фирдавсӣ асрро ном мебарад аммо дармеғ намеистад. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд бифаҳмӣ чаро Шоҳнома аз чор аср мегузарад.
